notes: Product faithful. Physics reads plausible: the braid passes in front of the barrel, the back half is hidden, and the hoop is wedged at a ~25 deg tilt halfway down with contact. Strictly, a ~13 mm opening could not have passed the 16.5 mm flange, but no viewer will read that.

fix: Same set-up, but stand the spool and hoops on pale blush handloom linen (never oatmeal, natural, undyed or sand linen) and lift the foreground shadow fill so it stays blush or ivory instead of going tan; keep a dusty-rose wall and a pale ivory sheer, with the curtain glow lower than the gold so the hoops are the brightest thing. Keep the faithful braid, disc and hinge. Optionally make the spool flanges only slightly wider than the barrel (about 14 mm) so the collar is physically possible.

reasons: Scale (rule 4): the charpai rope is drawn far too thin for the hoops. Each band is four thin twisted cords. One cord measures 45-52 px across perpendicular to its lay beside the lower hoop (seam profile from (1690,1540) to (1830,1700); ~46 px at (600-850,1600-1750)), or ~60-68 px corrected for the ~40 deg view. The lower hoop is 480 px across (x 1099-1580) and the standing hoop ~420 px tall (y ~1085-1505). Each hoop therefore spans ~7-10 rope widths instead of ~3, and the braid (~84 px radial) is thicker than a rope instead of thinner. Against the 8 mm rope the hoops read ~56-64 mm, about +125% to +155% vs 25 mm (at least +98% on the most conservative measure). Reading a whole 4-cord band as one 8 mm rope instead gives ~16 mm (-36%), so it is outside the 30% limit either way.

fix: Reshoot with ONE fat rope per pass instead of bundles of thin cords: 'each rope is a single soft 8 mm blush cotton rope, as thick as a pencil and visibly about 1.5x thicker than the hoop's braid; each band is at most two ropes side by side; each hoop spans only about three rope widths, and its 13 mm opening is narrower than two ropes; only about 12-15 cm of the woven top is in frame'. fix: Reshoot with blush-dyed warp threads (or ivory warp in front of a softly blurred blush plaster wall) and softer, less golden light, so no part of the frame goes tan or honey-beige.
